audit.why: Chart reads Camille, Skill, Singed, Singed, Camille, Singed, Singed on both layers and matches audits/top/camille__singed.json, the packet levelChart, and a 52.04% win rate over 955 games. Level 2-3 is where Hookshot arrives and level 6 is The Hextech Ultimatum; both are correctly marked.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears anywhere, and both the level-6 and 2-item spikes are argued against 'Insanity Potion regeneration' and 'Insanity Potion sustain'.
audit.why: Insanity Potion has no heal or regen in Riot's text — it grants combat stats and puts Grievous Wounds on Poison Trail. Hookshot is 16s at rank 1, longer than your own 10s Fling, so 'back off before her E is up' is impossible advice; Precision Protocol is 9s, Tactical Sweep 15s, The Hextech Ultimatum 140s.
audit.corrected: 16s Hookshot, 9s Precision Protocol, 140s ultimate and Singed's 17/10/100 written into the cooldown row, spikes and whys, and the fake regen replaced with the real anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'W-root-Fling combo' is named six times and does not exist — Mega Adhesive slows and GROUNDS, and the root only happens when Fling drops her in it. The grounding itself, which is the single most important interaction in the lane, is never mentioned: Hookshot is a dash, so a glued Camille has neither an engage nor an exit. Tactical Sweep's self-heal, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds against it, are also absent, as is Adaptive Defenses shielding against your poison's damage type.
audit.why: Riot text — Singed W: 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it'. Singed E: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' Camille E: 'pulls herself to a wall, leaping off'. Camille W: 'Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille.' Camille P: 'Basic attacks on champions grant a shield equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type' — so every auto she lands on you buys her a magic shield sized against your poison.
audit.corrected: Grounding, the real Fling-into-adhesive root, the Tactical Sweep heal versus Grievous Wounds, and the Adaptive Defenses magic shield are all stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing recorded about whether Fling can interrupt The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/camille.json carries 'channel' and 'untargetable' flags on the ultimate, but Riot's own description says only that she dashes to a target and anchors them — no channel, no untargetability. Per the rule that the description beats a misfiring derived flag, I asserted neither, and I did not repeat the _missing-interactions claim that Fling cancels it.

edits.before: Levels one and two are a concede. Camille's Q hits true damage on the second proc and her Hookshot stun arrives at level two before you have Mega Adhesive to respond — she can stick, proc Q twice, and disengage safely while you have no reliable way to root her in the cloud. Sit at the tip of Poison Trail range for CS, do not step forward to trade, and absolutely do not burn Fling because a wasted Fling with Hookshot still up means she punishes at will. Your only goal before level three is to not give first blood and get Mega Adhesive online.
edits.after: Levels one and two are a concede. Precision Protocol's re-cast lands true damage and Hookshot arrives at two before you have Mega Adhesive, so she can stick, proc Q twice and leave. Worse, Adaptive Defenses gives her a shield sized against your damage type every time she autos you, so your poison chip is doing less than the bar suggests. Sit at the tip of Poison Trail range for CS, do not step forward, and do not burn Fling — it is 10s and her Hookshot is 16s, so a wasted flip does not buy you the window you think it does. Reach level three without giving first blood.

edits.before: Once Mega Adhesive is on the ground the lane becomes a genuine read — you can root-Fling her if she walks into the goo chasing you, but she can also Hookshot the wall behind you to stun you out of the maneuver before it connects. At level six she holds The Hextech Ultimatum which is a hard counter to your run-at-you pattern: the cage shrinks your movement to irrelevance, and she burns through Insanity Potion regen with W true damage inside it. Respect her level-six all-in, proxy the wave instead of fighting her, and race toward Rylai's — the slow is the toolkit piece that makes her unable to simply sprint out of Poison Trail indefinitely.
edits.after: Once Mega Adhesive is on the ground the lane becomes a read, and the reason is the grounding: Hookshot is a wall-dash, so a Camille standing in your goo cannot engage and cannot leave. Glue her feet first, then Fling her back into the adhesive — landing in it is what roots her. She can still Hookshot the wall behind you before the vial lands, so throw it at her feet, not at the wall. At level six The Hextech Ultimatum answers your pattern: the arena shrinks your movement to nothing while Tactical Sweep's outer cone heals her through the poison. Pop Insanity Potion so its Grievous Wounds halves that heal, respect the all-in otherwise, and race to Rylai's so she can no longer sprint clear of the trail.

notes: 'W-root-Fling' is named six times and is not a real combo — Mega Adhesive grounds and slows, the root needs a Fling to land her inside it. The grounding, which switches Camille's only gap-closer and only escape off with one 1000-range vial, appeared nowhere on either layer. Also removed 'Insanity Potion regeneration' and 'Insanity Potion sustain'; Singed's R has no heal in Riot's text. UNVERIFIED and deliberately not written: champ-data/_kits/camille.json flags The Hextech Ultimatum as a channel and as untargetable, and _missing-interactions claims Fling cancels it outright. Riot's description supports neither, so I said nothing about it — this needs a human ruling before it goes on the page.
